bug_semantics: The MCP-exposed ado installer accepted an attacker-controlled package/command string and interpolated it without validation into Stata source. A value such as `outreg2\nshell touch /tmp/stata_mcp_ado_poc\n//` therefore introduced a second Stata statement; Stata's `shell`/`!` escape executed that statement as an OS command with the server user's privileges. In the advisory-era implementation, the default CLI selected profile `all`, `_TOOL_REGISTRY` included `ado_package_install` in `all`, the wrapper forwarded `package`, `SSC_Install.install()` formed `f"ssc install {package}{self.REPLACE_MESSAGE}"`, and `StataController.run()` delivered it to the interpreter. The guard blacklist did not protect this separate install path.
flaw_origin: The smallest true BIC is b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607, not the later installer-framework commit. Although titled as a directory-renaming refactor, b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607 independently added the complete `@mcp.tool(name="ssc_install")` entry point in `src/stata_mcp/__init__.py`: its unvalidated `command` argument was embedded into `write_dofile(f"ssc install {command}...")` and executed by `stata_do`. Commit 51e4bf3aff9e188de931ae77686bd42bc77524da merely moved that tool to `mcp_servers.py`; 0001cec1135824bc77dca6fe116ac6b06a2c8c4d later introduced the equivalently vulnerable `SSC_Install.install()` class; and 28e0757d5d0df5a9c6be257218e277dff332659e rewired/renamed the existing MCP tool to `ado_package_install`. Those later commits preserve or refactor an already exploitable flaw and are not the BIC.
ai_marker: Absent on the BIC commit object. `git cat-file commit b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607` shows author and committer `SongTan <sepinetam@gmail.com>`, one human-authored subject (`refactor: rename StataController and StataDo directories to snake_case naming convention`), and no body or trailers at all: no `Co-authored-by`, `Generated-with`, bot identity, or other AI attribution.
evidence: Advisory GHSA-49m4-vp58-wgc9/CVE-2026-55071 identifies unsanitized `package`, the SSC f-string, newline-to-`shell` RCE, affected range `<1.19.0`, and first patched 1.19.0. In the clone, `git log -L 630,653:src/stata_mcp/__init__.py b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607` shows b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607 adding all 24 lines of the decorated `ssc_install` tool, including both unvalidated f-strings and execution via `stata_do`; `git log --all --reverse -S 'def ssc_install' -- .` and `git log --all --reverse -S 'ssc install' -- .` cross-check that origin. Direct parent verification with `git grep -n -E 'ssc_install|ado_package_install|ssc install' 9ef0a4076b51955786a29afc7de4bb1c782b6faf -- src` returns no matches. `git show --find-renames 51e4bf3aff9e188de931ae77686bd42bc77524da` shows the later module extraction; `git log -L 12,17:src/stata_mcp/stata/builtin_tools/ado_install/ssc_install.py b2bc49ec447836e0b1d442ece472c42b7f78724b^` traces the later class sink to 0001cec1135824bc77dca6fe116ac6b06a2c8c4d, while `git show 28e0757d5d0df5a9c6be257218e277dff332659e` shows the wrapper rename/rewire. At tag v1.18.2, `git blame` confirms `mcp_servers.py:308-349` forwards `package`, `mcp_servers.py:626-632` places the tool in profile `all`, `cli/_handlers.py:295-300` defaults to `all`, and `ssc_install.py:15-16` constructs and runs the unvalidated command. The exact source fix is `git show b2bc49ec447836e0b1d442ece472c42b7f78724b`: it adds `validate_ado_package_name()` using a full-match identifier allowlist, invokes it both at API/MCP entry points and directly inside `SSC_Install.install()` before command construction, and includes a regression case `reghdfe\nshell echo pwn`; `git grep` on its parent still shows the naked f-string, while the fixed tree shows validation immediately before it. Commits 1641e93a71e7d1600adb2c7ab1041370d43347d4 and 7a00a338f0efd2c9b186a3923e6b56d8828db804 subsequently add opt-in/approval and narrower alphanumeric hardening but are not required to reject the reported newline payload. Tag checks are reproducible with `git tag --contains`: b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607 first appears in v1.7.0 (its parent describes to v1.6.3), so the precise vulnerable tagged interval is v1.7.0 through v1.18.2; b2bc49ec447836e0b1d442ece472c42b7f78724b first appears in v1.19.0. Tag v1.19.0 resolves to 29f406a66ccbf60d23602584ce4c397af3e5c94d, and the first-party release page labels it a Security release and explicitly lists command-injection input validation, unsafe-profile isolation, approval, and bypass closure. Finally, `git cat-file commit b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607` reproduces the BIC-only marker absence and human author/committer identity.
reasoning: The vulnerability existed as soon as b61cd574b86bb6aa3a931ed637de0fb66ce82607 added a default MCP tool that wrote its caller-controlled string as executable Stata source; changing the delivery from a generated do-file to `StataController.run()` and renaming the tool did not create the missing trust-boundary validation. The direct parent has no installer tool or matching command construction, making parent absence proven. The first affected release is therefore v1.7.0 even though the advisory's ecosystem range is conservatively stated as all versions below 1.19.0. b2bc49ec447836e0b1d442ece472c42b7f78724b is the smallest direct closing fix for this CVE because its full-match package validation rejects newlines at every public and direct-loader path before interpolation; the remaining June 7 hardening reduces exposure and tightens policy. AI attribution is judged only from the BIC commit object. That object identifies SongTan and contains no AI marker or trailer, so the closed verdict is NOT_AI regardless of any AI-associated work elsewhere in repository history.
